one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-01 very likely contains Q3 FY26 results: FormFactor reported Q3 on Oct 29, 2025 and Oct 30, 2024, so expect about Oct 28-29, 2026 after the close. The Q3 guide is $270M +/- $10M revenue and $0.86 non-GAAP EPS. The company beat its own Q2 guide on every line and the stock rose 26.6% on that print. But the stock has already run from about $100 (Aug) and $119 (Sep 22) to about $148-149, partly on Deutsche Bank's Sep 30 Buy initiation ($200 target, second-source Nvidia/TSMC GPU probe cards). A beat is largely expected, and the Q4 guide decides the reaction, which could be +/-15-25% either way. Short-term regularities point in opposite directions: momentum (the post-earnings drift seen after Q2) against reversal after a sharp analyst-driven jump with RSI near 72. Net effect: a symmetric, slightly wide distribution centred on today's price, with sigma about 21% for the month (85% annual vol / 3.5 = 24%, trimmed a little because part of the realized vol came from one-off re-rating jumps). The brief gives the last close as $147.90; another feed shows $149.15. That difference does not change the ladder materially.

fair_value.method: A blend of forward P/E (forward NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 of about $4.50 x 32x = $144, weight 0.7) and EV/sales (forward revenue of about $1.30B x 7x plus about $0.33B net cash over about 80M diluted shares = $118, weight 0.3). Result: about $136, roughly 8% below the current price.

The current price implies about 10-11x run-rate sales, a record for FORM. Its 2021 and 2024 peaks (about $45-60 on about $0.75-0.8B of sales and 77M shares) implied about 4-6x. 7x credits structurally higher margins but assumes some mean reversion.

bear.story: A semi-test cycle rollover, as in 2022 and 2024-25: HBM/DRAM capex digestion or an AI capex pause. NTM EPS falls to about $2.8 and the multiple derates to about 25x. FORM fell about 55% from its monthly peak in both prior cycles (Feb-2021 $45 to Oct-2022 $20; Jun-2024 $60.5 to Apr-2025 $28).

base.story: Growth continues at a decelerating pace. NTM EPS of about $4.3-4.5 at about 32-34x, which lets the elevated multiple compress while earnings catch up.

bull.story: The Nvidia second-source probe-card ramp hits Deutsche Bank's 2028 path early, HBM4 test intensity rises and co-packaged optics systems scale. EPS reaches about $5.5 at 40x+ and momentum continues (in one study, stocks that doubled rose again the next year 53% of the time).

thesis_break_reason: $88 is about 40% below today and below the Aug-2026 trough of about $100. At about 25x it implies NTM EPS of about $3.5 or less, i.e. no growth from the Q3 run-rate. Trading there would most likely mean an order or guidance cut (HBM/DRAM digestion, a lost or delayed Nvidia/TSMC qualification, or gross-margin reversal from the 53% level) rather than ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Why FORM jumped on Sep 30: no 8-K or company release was filed around Sep 30 (EDGAR list shows only Form 4/144 since the Aug 4 10-Q). The roughly 10% jump from $136.25 to about $149 came from Deutsche Bank initiating at Buy with a $200 target. The thesis was FormFactor becoming the second qualified probe-card source for Nvidia GPUs made at TSMC: a TAM of about $0.5B, about 20% share and more than $200M of sales by 2028, plus HBM sales near $400M by 2028. The move came during a broad chip rebound and the company's investor summit; the CEO's planned sales (Form 4) did not hurt. Fundamentals: Q2 FY26 delivered record revenue of $258M, non-GAAP GM of 53.3% and EPS of $0.82, and Q3 is guided to $270M and $0.86. Annualized that is about $3.45, so at $148 the stock trades at about 43x run-rate and about 39x my NTM estimate. Base rates: (1) FORM's own history shows two roughly 55% peak-to-trough drawdowns in 2021-22 and 2024-25, and monthly closes moved from $160 to $100 and back to $149 within 2026 alone. (2) Large gains are followed by roughly coin-flip next-year direction: the patternsite study puts continuation at 53% for stocks that doubled, and for the index, gains above 50% were followed by negative years about 65% of the time, per A Wealth of Common Sense. (3) The 5-year forward P/E averages about 36x and peers trade at 20-37x. (4) Macro: Kalshi prices a 2027 US recession at about 20-22% (KXRECSSNBER-27, about 542k contracts traded) and a 2026 recession at 5%. My fair value is about $136, slightly below spot. I set the median 12-month outcome at about $140, roughly -5%, because a stretched multiple offsets strong earnings momentum. The spread is lognormal-like with sigma about 0.62, below the 85% realized vol because part of that came from one-off re-rating, and I fattened the left tail for cyclical-crash risk (P(<$59) about 9.5%). Scenario mean is about $148. Research was limited: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable, and consensus pages found were stale, so the EPS path is my own estimate built from guidance. No option data was used.
